author: Mark Atwood
text:
Survey of every SQLite connection and pragma in the workspace, 2026-11-27.

Nothing in production code opens a connection per operation. The
hypothesis in this bead's description is false for the code as it
stands, and these are the facts behind that:

- mimid-server, crates/mimid-server/src/store/mod.rs, two sqlx pools
  built once per process by Store::open (called once, from main.rs:171;
  every other caller is a test). The writer pool is pinned:
  max_connections(1), min_connections(1), idle_timeout(None),
  max_lifetime(None). The read-only pool took sqlx's defaults:
  max_connections 10, min_connections 0, idle_timeout 10 minutes,
  max_lifetime 30 minutes, so an established read connection was closed
  after ten idle minutes or thirty of life and the next query opened one
  on the caller's path. That is the one defect found, and it is fixed:
  four read connections, opened by Store::open, retired by nothing.
- The agent holds four long-lived rusqlite connections, one per purpose,
  each opened once: the MLS/state connection (mimi_mls::Store::open
  through mimid-agent-core state.rs mls_store, from Agent::new),
  mimid-agent-store's Database (store.rs open_database, daemon.rs:250),
  Credentials (daemon.rs:206, and once per admin CLI command in
  cli.rs:69) and Push. Each sets secure_delete and busy_timeout once on
  its own connection. No pool, and none needed: rusqlite connections are
  serialized behind the mutex that owns them.
- mimi-mls has no pragmas of its own and no I/O beyond the connection it
  is handed or opens once.

Where the logged statement comes from: sqlx turns SqliteConnectOptions'
pragmas into one statement and runs it in ConnectOptions::connect, after
sqlite3_open (sqlx-sqlite-0.9.0 src/options/connect.rs:39 and
pragma_string at :72). Setting journal_mode and foreign_keys through the
connect options, which the code already did, is what produces
"PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL; PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON; ". sqlx offers no
way to apply them during open, so the fix shape this bead proposed was
already in place and cannot be improved that way. The cost is per
connection opened, which is why retiring connections mattered.

The 2.4 seconds: journal_mode = WAL on a database not yet in WAL takes
an exclusive lock and fsyncs the header, and sqlite3_busy_timeout does
not cover that lock (sqlx-sqlite options/mod.rs:181). Every test makes a
fresh database, so every start in a gate run pays the conversion; a
deployed provider pays it once ever. On an already-WAL database SQLite
returns the current mode without taking the lock.

Not countable, and why: the defect was a retirement policy, and
retirement needs ten real minutes. sqlx's reaper ages connections with
std::time::Instant (sqlx-core pool/inner.rs:22), so tokio::time::pause
and advance wake the reaper's sleep but leave every connection's age at
zero and nothing is reaped. What is countable is the pool's own census,
Pool::size, which equals the number of connections opened because none
is retired: the regression test
(store::tests::queries_open_no_connection) runs twenty concurrent reads
and twenty writes and asserts the census does not move. Before the fix
it moved from 1 to 10 and the test failed.

Left alone, for a human decision: the agent's mimid.sqlite has no
journal_mode set anywhere, so it is in SQLite's DELETE mode with four
connections of the same process writing it. A writer there excludes
every reader, each commit fsyncs the journal, the file and the
directory, and the losers wait out a 10 second busy timeout. WAL would
end the exclusion, but it keeps a deleted row's old page in the -wal
file until a checkpoint, which weakens the secure_delete guarantee of
bead mimid-1vul.9 (agent-frontends.md 7.9). Bead mimid-604m.4.
